articles.title_orig: Hacked emails yield revelations on Germany's far-right AfD party leader
articles.title_zh: Hacked emails yield revelations on Germany's far-right AfD party leader
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed. Below is a round-up of top stories from and about Germany on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.
Alice Weidel, the co-leader of Germany's far-right AfD, is expected to present her party's policy for the EU at the European Parliament on Wednesday.
According to a report from news outlet Politico , the AfD policy paper on the EU does not seek to exit the bloc or the eurozone at first.
The party rather wants to downsize the EU's powers and budget.
Instead of direct European Parliament elections, the AfD would like to see delegates appointed by national parliaments. The AfD would also limit the scope of the European Commission to purely administrative tasks and supplant the European Court of Justice with an arbitration tribunal.
The AfD would threaten to slash Germany's contributions to the EU budget.
Germany under the AfD would seek exemptions from EU regulations regarding issues such as migration and social policy. The AfD may also seek opt-outs of other areas such as agriculture and financial policies.
If the EU would not bend to the AfD's demands for reform, the party would then seek a German referendum on EU membership.
A referendum would be unrealistic, as it would require a constitutional amendment to the German Basic Law to take place. An amendment would require a two-thirds majority vote in both the Bundestag and upper house Bundesrat — an extremely high threshold to meet.
The AfD hopes that it can implement its EU policies in 2029, when the next German and European elections will take place.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Recent German federal election surveys show the AfD in first place but it would have to form a coalition with another partner to establish a ruling majority government. That's difficult when other parties such as the conservative Christian Democratic Union refuse to have any cooperation with the AfD as part of a "firewall" policy .
More than 421,000 emails linked to Germany's far-right AfD have been published following a cyberattack (see additional entry below).
The alleged material includes private communications, sensitive personal data and reported references to racism, antisemitism and Nazi ideology, although much of the trove has not yet been independently verified.
Could this become one of the biggest political data leaks in modern German history?
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
A German supermarket is getting attention online after responding to a customer who objected to its diverse workforce.
Nine pro-Palestinian protesters seeking an end to Western arms exports to Israel glued themselves to the ground in front of a Berlin facility belonging to German weapons manufacturer Rheinmetall.
Berlin police responded to the incident at 5:30 a.m. (0330 UTC) with 11 protesters at the site. The "Peacefully Against Genocide" group was behind the action.
The factory began arms production in June. It is involved in the production of shell casings for artillery ammunition and parts for kamikaze drones, according to local public broadcaster RBB.
It is unclear how much the facility in Berlin's Wedding neighborhood is involved with weapons for Israel. Rheinmetall, however, is Germany's largest arms manufacturer.
In the western German state of Hesse, seven people also blocked the entry to the Rheinmetall facility in the city of Kassel, according to local police.
In addition, demonstrators against weapons exports glued themselves in front of a weapons company in the western city of Kaiserslautern.
Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was looking into the theft and subsequent online publication of emails stolen by unidentified hackers during a cyberattack last month.
An AfD spokesperson said the hackers had targeted a hosting provider used by the party and appeared to have copied data from a small number of mostly inactive email accounts.
"The recent online publication of what is presumably a portion of this data is currently being investigated," the spokesperson said. "A preliminary assessment can only be provided once this investigation has been concluded."
Although the spokesperson did not say how much data was stolen, an earlier report by the mass-circulation daily Bild put the number of AfD-linked emails published at more than 420,000.
According to Bild , the material published included not only emails sent by party figures such as co-leader Alice Weidel but also bank statements, academic certificates and membership lists.
The website hosting the material was offline by Tuesday afternoon.
However, archived versions showed a volume of 281 gigabytes of data under the headline "The party's own records, unedited."
The emails and other materials published have not yet been certified as authentic by any independent body.
The AfD, several state chapters of which have been classified as "confirmed right-wing extremist" by regional branches of Germany's domestic intelligence agency, has been topping recent national opinion polls and made gains in recent state elections .
Some politicians and civil society groups have called for it to be banned, arguing that the party is a threat to democracy, an accusation the party has rejected.
While Berlin hosts a summit on investment in Germany, an increasing amount of US capital is flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses.
As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.
Read all the details here: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
German economic confidence — like that across the eurozone in general — deteriorated in October, according to experts at the Mannheim-based Center for European Economic Research (ZEW).
The ZEW's monthly economic confidence index fell to a three-month low on Tuesday, down to 28.1 from 34.7 in September. That is nearly two points lower than forecast.
"Private consumption and investment remain weak because of high energy prices: They put real incomes under pressure, increase production costs and keep inflation higher for longer," said ZEW President Achim Wambach.
"The German economy," added Wambach, "is slowly emerging from stagnation, but the recovery is not self-sustaining."
The biggest losers in this latest index were banks, insurers, the service sector and the telecommunications industry.
Winners were seen in the metal manufacturing and electronics industries.
ZEW compiles its monthly surveys from interviews with banking, insurance and financial industry experts and businesses on their expectations for economic and capital market developments.
The ZEW's index is considered a key indicator for Germany's economic development.
Tuesday's survey was based on interviews with 178 analysts between October 12 and 19, 2026.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz has indulged in an abundance of the most common cliches about his country and compatriots while trying to portray Germany as the ideal place to do business at an investment summit.
"Germans are hardworking, going to bed early, rising before dawn," he told the domestic and international guests at the Invest in Germany Summit.
"Worst traffic is in the morning between 6 and 7," he said.
"On holidays, we are first on the beach, spreading towels before breakfast. If we agree on delivery dates, we stick to it. If you invite friends from Germany for dinner at 7, we will arrive at 6:58.
"We are reliable, predictable, precise, and unsurprising," the chancellor continued. "We are, in short, what investors like most."
Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil also used blunt humor in his appeal to potential investors, saying in his speech simply: "I want your money."
Both pitches appear to have succeeded, with investment commitments worth billions made at the summit.

articles.title_zh: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors
articles.content_orig:

Helium producers in the United States will gain access to more federal financing and the government will keep a closer watch on the gas after the Energy Department designated it a critical material on Friday.
The Energy Department said the designation was made because helium is indispensable for making semiconductors that are essential to energy generation, and because the global supply is at risk of disruption.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Trump administration is freeing America from reliance on foreign sources of critical materials, strengthening domestic manufacturing, supporting American jobs and securing the materials essential to U.S. economic and national security.
“President Trump is bringing back America’s manufacturing industry, and that means making sure we have the materials needed to build things in America again,” Wright said in a statement.
Helium is the 20th critical material identified by the department. Metallurgical coal used for steelmaking was the last substance to be added to the list, in 2025. Fluorine is the only other gas on it.
To qualify, a non-fuel mineral element or substance must serve an essential function in one or more energy technologies, and there must be a high risk of disruption to the supply chain.
The designation matters for reasons that go well beyond party balloons, even though helium is what makes them rise. The department points to the gas's role in wind, solar and nuclear energy production, space exploration, medical imaging and research.
Assistant Secretary of Energy Audrey Robertson said helium's unique properties make it irreplaceable, citing the facts that it is non-combustible and has the lowest boiling point of any gas. Robertson, who oversees the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, added that the nation needs an ample supply for semiconductors, quantum and super computing, and superconducting magnets.
“We need to make sure that we can build those here. And helium is one of those components that could be a single point of failure, where we cannot let that happen. That’s why we’re designating it within our statutory authority, but I think why it’s important is not necessarily for our birthday parties,” Robertson said in an interview. “It’s really towards the future of American competitiveness and energy security, which we believe is national security.”
The supply risks behind the designation are concentrated abroad. Qatar's helium exports have been severely curtailed by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a result of its war with Israel and the U.S.
Iranian strikes on Qatar's infrastructure have also affected supply. Russia, one of the other top helium producers alongside the United States, imposed temporary export controls on helium in April to protect its domestic supply.
The United States is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, and helium is primarily produced as a byproduct of natural gas processing. Even so, U.S. output is constrained.
The country produced 81 million cubic meters of helium in 2025, or 43% of the global supply, and exported 38 million cubic meters of that. Annual production has run at roughly 80 million cubic meters since 2021.
Large reserves sit in Wyoming, Kansas, Texas, Oklahoma, Colorado and Utah. But according to the department, helium extraction plants are at their limits, and it takes years to permit and build new ones, which continues to constrain U.S. production.
Federal data shows the plants extracting the most helium, as of 2023, were located in Kansas, Texas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Oklahoma. The constraints have a historical dimension.
The United States once kept a strategic national stockpile of helium in Texas, much like the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Congress mandated in 2013 that it be privatized, and the Bureau of Land Management completed the sale of the federal helium system to the industrial gas company Messer in 2024.
Some in the helium industry had urged the government to make the designation formal. The North American gas exploration company Avanti Helium Corp. says it is urgent, and that an increase in North American supply is needed to avoid becoming dependent on foreign sources.
The U.S. Geological Survey included helium on a 2018 list of critical minerals, but later lists omitted it because the domestic supply of helium was considered secure. The United States designates both critical minerals and critical materials, and there is some crossover between the two lists.
Greeshma Gadikota, director of the Lenfast Center for Sustainable Energy at Columbia University, said that despite environmental concerns with recovering helium from natural gas, there are also opportunities.
“If we burn the natural gas, there are a lot of CO2 emissions associated with that,” Gadikota said. "But if you just extract the helium and use it, the uses of it don't contribute necessarily to greenhouse gas emissions.
“So from a climate standpoint, if we are going to continue down the line of extracting natural gas and recovering helium," she added, “I would prefer to see natural gas being used in a form where we directly produce hydrogen and we produce solid carbon.” Hydrogen is a clean burning fuel, and solid carbon can provide permanent carbon sequestration.
“We can effectively consolidate everything from raw materials to finished product in terms of manufacturing in the United States and rely less on overseas,” Gadikota said. "It brings more refining, recovery, use capabilities to the U.S. and actually justifies any investments of U.S. taxpayer dollars in initiatives related to helium production and refining."

articles.title_orig: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.title_zh: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.
Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.
Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.
For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.
Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.
Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.
Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.
Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .
Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.
Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.
The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

articles.title_orig: Carney says AtkinsRealis is a contender to build nuclear power plant in Turkey
articles.title_zh: Carney says AtkinsRealis is a contender to build nuclear power plant in Turkey
articles.content_orig:
NATO allies Canada and Turkey upgraded their relations to a "strategic partnership" during the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister on Thursday, as Mark Carney seeks new global trade partners to reduce reliance on the United States.
The agreement by Carney and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan marks a significant thaw in diplomatic ties that had long been cool over Canadian concerns over human rights and a past embargo on sending weapons to Turkey.
The new partnership signed in Ankara focuses on trade and investment, defense and security, energy, and social and diplomatic ties. It aims to create jobs and opportunities for Canadian and Turkish companies to do more business together.
Carney is on a global trade blitz that he hopes will help buffer Canada from a trade war with the US, where President Donald Trump has applied sweeping tariffs and questioned the neighboring country's sovereignty.
Speaking next to Erdogan at Turkey's presidential palace, Carney said the strategic partnership would have four pillars and include a three-year action plan.
"We've planted the seeds of something new: a strategic partnership that will create new opportunities for our workers and businesses, and greater security and prosperity for both our peoples. With care and commitment, it will grow for generations to come," Carney said.
At the ceremony, Canadian and Turkish ministers signed cooperation deals on energy, defense and air transport.
Turkey, a major emerging market economy and regional military power, is seeking new investment and collaboration for its burgeoning defense industry, new nuclear power plants and mining sector.
Erdogan, who has led Turkey for 23 years, praised Carney as a leader with "common sense and acumen" on the world political stage.
"Today, we have alleviated the long-standing Turkey-Canada disconnect. Now, we are starting a new era between Turkey and Canada," Erdogan said. The two sides expect to raise their trade volume from $3 billion first to $5 billion and then to $10 billion, he said, without giving a timeframe.
Canadian and Turkish negotiators will kick off the first round of free trade talks next month in Ankara, Carney said, adding that Export Development Canada and Turkey's Eximbank would sign a new deal to boost companies' cooperation on projects in third nations.
Carney referenced the need to move forward with Turkey amid the "rupture" and "new world order," though neither he nor Erdogan mentioned the United States. Carney will meet prominent Turkish business leaders and investors in Istanbul on Friday.
In the energy sector, Canada and Turkey pledged to ramp up collaboration in areas such as nuclear energy, critical minerals, and liquefied natural gas.
Reuters first reported this week that the countries planned to sign a declaration deepening cooperation in the four areas outlined on Thursday.
Although trade between Canada and Turkey is tiny, Turkey accounted for less than 0.3% of Canada’s total merchandise trade, or C$4.34 billion ($3.09 billion); bilateral trade has risen nearly 50% in the past five years.
Still, Canada sends nearly 70% of exports to the US.
"This trip is part of the geopolitical necessity of signaling to Americans that we are not sitting around waiting for them," said Bessma Momani, professor of political science at the University of Waterloo.
In the last year, Canada has signed more than 20 trade deals as part of Carney’s push to double non-US exports in the next decade. This included a trip to China to reset fractured relations, which was criticized because Canadian authorities previously said Beijing had interfered in at least two federal elections. China says it does not interfere in other countries' internal affairs.
Turkey's crackdown on the opposition since 2024 and new arrests targeting the LGBTQ+ community since September have drawn criticism from rights groups and some European officials. Ankara says the judiciary is independent, denying that investigations or court cases are politically motivated.
Carney has focused less on rights than his predecessors, analysts say.
"Carney will have to walk a very fine line in Turkey between opening new economic possibilities for Canada while trying to maintain Canada's middle power role in fighting for equality," said Anna Agathangelou, a professor of politics at York University.
At the NATO leaders' summit in July, Carney and Erdogan launched negotiations for a free-trade agreement, and Turkey also agreed to join Canada’s Defense, Security and Resilience Bank as a founding member.
Turkey has held talks with Canadian engineering firm AtkinsRealis as well as South Korea's ​Korea Electric Power Corporation and China's State Power Investment Corporation about potentially building its planned second and third nuclear power plants.
In 2024, Canada removed weapons-export controls on Turkey, including on optical ​technology used in drones that Turkey exports to dozens of nations. Canada mainly exports lentils, aircraft and electronics to Turkey, and imports ​medical devices, fishing vessels, aircraft engines and jewelry.

articles.title_orig: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.title_zh: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.content_orig:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
In an interview with the Daily Mail, Markle Sr denied possessing child sexual abuse images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.
It is understood that authorities in the UK previously told Meghan that allegations made about her father in a 2018 letter sent to Scotland Yard, and subsequently shared with her by the police, were being investigated.
Meghan was informed by the Met of the allegations in the summer shortly after her wedding, it is believed.
In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan said: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.
“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection [Rasp]. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”
The 2018 letter was understood to have been shared with Meghan by the Rasp unit within the Met police.
It is understood the Met has not previously investigated Markle Snr, nor is it currently doing so. The force said it was making internal inquiries regarding officers from Rasp being involved in the passing on of a letter.
A Met spokesperson said: “We are aware of media reports that officers from the Met’s royalty and specialist protection command were involved in the passing on of a letter in 2018. We are undertaking inquiries internally in an effort to confirm this.”
Markle Sr has been estranged from the duchess since he failed to attend her wedding to Prince Harry on health grounds, and he has never met his grandchildren Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.
The Sun reported that Markle Jr told detectives in the Philippines he had discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sexual abuse images on computers and mobile phones stored in four large boxes at the home in Cebu where Markle Sr was living until he returned to the US in May after having a stroke.
Markle Jr, 60, said he had also contacted the FBI in the US, the Sun reported.
The undersecretary for the Philippines’ justice department, Nicholas Ty, told the BBC the matter was being investigated by a human trafficking and child sexual exploitation taskforce in Cebu.
The interior secretary, Jonvic Remulla, separately told the BBC that national police had secured Markle Sr’s computer to conduct a comprehensive digital forensic examination. Remulla said it would take “one week to get the forensic [results]”.
Meghan’s father has denied possessing child sexual abuse images, telling the Daily Mail that the accusations were “sick lies”.
He told the newspaper that the computers had not been in his possession since he left Rosarito, Mexico, with his son in January 2025 and moved to the Philippines “for a fresh start”.
Speaking from a rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk with a prosthetic limb after his left leg was amputated because of a blood clot, he told the Mail: “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.
“This is bullshit. It’s just a bunch of lies. It’s sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”
Meghan’s half-sister Samantha Markle has defended their father, accusing her brother Markle Jr of “making up lies” to make money.
She told the Mail: “There is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever and my brother is disgusting for making them up. He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
She alleged her brother made the allegations days after their father cut off his funds, “and once the money stopped he made up the most outrageous lies he could to make money from the media”.
She alleged the computers were not in her father’s possession for two years and he could have been set up. “That leaves a lot of room for tampering,” she said.

articles.title_orig: MTA suspending bus fare enforcement teams after altercations emerge
articles.title_zh: MTA suspending bus fare enforcement teams after altercations emerge
articles.content_orig:
Make your contribution now and help Gothamist thrive in 2026. Donate today
Gothamist is funded by sponsors and member donations
The MTA is temporarily shutting down its bus fare enforcement teams after a Brooklyn school dean was roughed up by agents who suspected he hadn’t paid , MTA Chair Janno Lieber announced at a news conference Thursday, adding that a second incident had also come to his attention.
The MTA will review safety protocols while the so-called EAGLE teams are taken off the street. Lieber shared few details about the second incident, but said it raised similar questions about whether the agents involved had shared timely, accurate information about the altercation with supervisors.
“I was not happy that leadership of the MTA and even New York City Transit didn’t even hear about that episode until more than a week afterwards. It now appears that there is another episode where that failure to timely report is even more extreme. The incident that's come to attention is now several months old and it didn’t come up,” Lieber said.
“I’m not willing to keep our teams active in the field until I know that all protocols are being followed with respect to both the customer interactions, how they’re conducted, but also with respect to the reporting and investigation of incidents … As a result I’m ordering an immediate safety stand-down until these investigations conclude,” he added.
Lieber has previously said the EAGLE teams, who scan bus tickets and issue fines to fare-beaters, are critical to reducing rampant fare evasion on buses. MTA statistics show as much as half of bus riders skip the fare.
But a video of a confrontation between EAGLE agents and Mott Bridges Academy dean Kyle Taylor prompted questions about the conduct of the teams enforcing $3 rides.
Video showed agents pinned Taylor against a bus and slammed him to the ground after they asked if he paid his fare on a B14 bus in Brownsville. He sustained injuries to his back, neck, shoulder, arm and elbow.
The MTA suspended the agents involved while it began investigating the incident. Taylor maintains he did pay for the fare after transferring from a different bus, where he received a transfer ticket.
An EAGLE officer filed official paperwork reporting that Taylor “fell out of the bus” and refused medical attention, an account contradicted by the video footage.
Taylor’s lawyer Benjamin Pinczewski called for a complete dissolution of the unit. “ It disproportionately subjects people of color to this kind of treatment, and it's unacceptable,” Pinczewski said.
“We’re going to take a break, and take another look and we’ll be back when we’ve completed that,” Lieber added.
Jeremy Edwards, a spokesperson for Mayor Zohran Mamdani, praised the move.
“No New Yorker should fear for their safety because they cannot afford the fare. We welcome the MTA’s decision to suspend fare enforcement while it investigates reports of excessive force by members of its fare collection teams. Our transit system should make life easier, not harder,” Edwards said.

articles.title_orig: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
Arcane Journal – The River of Bones is packed with new background and rules. Having learnt about the lore earlier in the week, we sat down with the Warhammer: The Old World studio to discover more about the rules.
JTY: There’s a wealth of new content in this Arcane Journal, both for Tomb Kings of Khemri and Wood Elf Realms players, as well as magic items and battlefield rules for everyone. But you won’t need this supplement in order to use the new Tomb Kings models – the profiles for all of those can be found in Ravening Hordes .*
Dave: Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new scenarios. The first is a multi-player Battle March scenario for four players, and the second recreates the battle on the banks of the Crystal Mere, the mysterious lake in the heart of Athel Loren where the Tomb Kings and Wood Elves clashed. Alongside these is a really fun table of rules for Enchanted Terrain , the type of thing a traveller might encounter in the depths of Athel Loren. This can be good or bad depending on what you roll. A low roll might see a unit covered in Clawing Mud suffer modifiers to its Movement, or fall subject to Stupidity due to a Fungal Enchantment . But a high roll can result in a unit gaining Regeneration after discovering the Waters of Rejuvenation , or getting a Ward save after securing the Blessings of the Ancient Wood .
JTY: In the Champions of Nehekhara section you’ll find new rules for using the Tomb Kings of Khemri in games of Battle March. For example, the Arch Hierophant enables players to field a Battle March army without having to have a Hierophant on the battlefield. Instead, the army is empowered by the machinations of a more distant Liche Priest. This gives more freedom when writing your muster list because you aren’t obliged to include two characters, whilst still allowing you to resurrect slain models as normal. Although, of course, this is not without risk…
Dave: Speaking of muster lists, Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new Armies of Infamy. The first focuses on the Tomb Kings themselves, in particular the Barrow Kingdoms. These are the long forgotten vassal states of ancient Nehekhara, the fringes of a vast empire conquered in Settra’s lifetime, where occupying armies merged with those of barbarian warlords keen to emulate the practices of Nehekhara in everything from religion and burial rites to organising an army.
Where this army differs from the norm is in the options. Liche Priests gain access to the Lores of Battle Magic and Dark Magic , the better to represent the sorts of shaman common in these ancient realms, whilst both Skeleton Horsemen and Skeleton Chariots** can be upgraded, making them the ideal hard-hitting bodyguard to accompany a long dead scion of the Great Land.
JTY: But that’s not all, there’s also an Army of Infamy for the Wood Elf Realms, the Spirits of the Forest. This army focuses on the more magical elements of Athel Loren, encouraging armies that contain lots of Dryads, Treekin and Treemen. In terms of special rules, the list gives players access to Blessings of the Elder Wood , a number of magical upgrades for their Treemen and Branchwraiths , effectively giving them access to their own unique magic items.
This is followed by rules for Wood Elf Kindreds, the various clans associated with different parts of the great forest. These reflect how Kinbands, or units, from different Kindreds fight. The Kinbands of Cavaroc , for example, gain Vanguard, whilst the Kinbands of Torgovann get to choose a non-magical combat weapon and improve its AP.
The Kinbands of Cavaroc (+15 points per unit)
Kinbands that hail from the open plains of Cavaroc are swift of foot, capable of covering vast distances in a single march.
A unit belonging to this Kindred gains the Vanguard special rule and improves the Movement characteristic of the unit and their mounts (should they have one) by 1.
The Kinbands Of Torgovann (+1 points per model)
Sharing their realm with the Forge of Starlight, the Kindreds of Torgovann are armed with the finest weapons to be found in Athel Loren.
Choose one non-magical combat weapon wielded by this unit and improve the Armour Piercing characteristic of that weapon by 1. The chosen weapon must be clearly noted on your muster list.
Dave: Finally, there is a brand new set of common magic items, this time themed around the sort of ancient artefact that might be found in the depths of a long-forgotten barrow mound somewhere in the foothills of the Vaults of the Grey Mountains.
As usual, this section includes magic weapons, armour, talismans and banners, as well as enchanted and arcane items, all of which are very useful, but many of which bear an unfortunate curse!*** Take the Armour of Dust , for example; this suit of full plate armour reduces the wearer’s Toughness if they roll a 1 when making an armour save. Or there’s the vial of Barrow Dirt , a single-use item which the bearer can throw at the enemy like a Breath Weapon, with Strength 3, an AP of -3 and Multiple Wounds (2). However, if they fail an Initiative test after doing so, they risk being hit as well.
Vials of dust scraped from the floor of ancient tombs can desiccate the flesh and sap the strength of those they come into contact with.
0-1 per model. Single use. Barrow-dirt is a breath weapon with the following profile:
Breath Weapon, Magical Attacks, Multiple Wounds (2)
Notes: After using Barrow-dirt, the bearer must make an Initiative test. If this test is failed, they risk being hit as if they were partially under the flame template.
Thanks, folks! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order tomorrow, along with the Host of Nehekhara Army Reinforcement Set. There’s never been a better time to start an implacable undead army or to grow your existing legions.
* But don’t forget to keep your eyes on the latest FAQ and Errata . ** The new Skeleton Chariots are on a different base size compared to the old kits – download the PDF errata now. *** That’s on you for taking mysterious magic items from forgotten barrow mounds.

articles.title_orig: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.title_zh: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.content_orig:
Show features live chat sessions with breeders, a podcast and updates on dogs’ progress from birth to weigh-ins
A 24-hour Finnish TV show dedicated entirely to the live progress of a dog and her six newborn puppies is drawing millions of viewers.
As well as a 24-hour webcam, Pentulive (Puppy Live) includes live evening chat sessions with the dogs’ breeder, a podcast and an instant notification service that updates followers on the puppies’ progress – from their birth to weigh-ins and first nail trims – for eight weeks.
This is the sixth season of the hit show by the broadcaster Yle, and the latest contribution to the growing Nordic cultural phenomenon of “slow TV”.
The trend started in Norway in 2009 with Bergensbanen, a seven-hour train journey broadcast on NRK , and was followed in Sweden by SVT’s Den stora älgvandringen (The Great Moose Migration), which features unnarrated glimpses of moose from the north of the country making their annual journey to summer grazing grounds.
Pentulive has long attracted interest from outside Finland, but this year it is also being broadcast in Sweden (under the name Valparna live ). Yle recently announced that it had also sold the format to a broadcaster in the Netherlands.
Ville Alijoki, the editorial manager of Yle’s factual journalism, said: “There’s a certain magic to it, something that people miss when this world is sometimes quite dark.”
On Saturday, the lagotto romagnolo puppies – four male and two female – will mark their two-week birthday by being officially named after a vote by viewers. Among the nominations are Martha, Timo, Ronja and Dante.
In mid-December, the puppies will leave their mother, Hilkka, and be adopted by new families.
Yle said the current season of Pentulive was on a path to break previous viewing records. Across its first two weeks, the stream has been watched for more than 1m hours, and the show has attracted 1.85 million unique viewers across all related content.
Fans say the puppies offer a relaxing break from work, and comfort from stress, loneliness and illness.
after newsletter promotion
Pirjo Koskinen, a science journalist who came up with the Pentulive concept with the aim of educating viewers on the latest dog research and the importance of the first few weeks of a dog’s life, said the show provided “relief from the terrible things happening in the world”.
She said: “Wars, bombing, climate change, habitat loss etc make us anxious and you can escape, for at least a moment, by watching the canine family.”
Watching the mother and breeder take care of the puppies was like watching “a loop of love and caring”, she said.
“It’s real and we are in the basics of life: the miracle of birth, growth and development. It’s so heartwarming to see eyes opening and first clumsy steps, and it’s happening right now. That brings us joy, but also many funny moments during eight weeks.”

(Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Thursday, as renewed Middle East tensions sent crude oil prices higher, reinforcing inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. A sharp selloff in technology shares and falling Treasury yields failed to generate sustained safe-haven demand for bullion, while silver faced additional pressure from concerns about industrial demand and slowing economic activity. At the time of the latest verified late-afternoon reading, spot gold was trading near $4,021.20 an ounce, down $119.10, or 2.88%, while spot silver was trading near $54.440, down $3.410, or 5.90%.
Market positioning remains divided between persistent inflation pressure, weaker economic activity and growing financial-market instability. September consumer inflation increased 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually , while producer prices rose 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively . Fed funds futures continue to favor no change at the Oct. 27-28 Federal Reserve meeting, with recent pricing indicating approximately an 84% probability of a pause and a 16% probability of a 25-basis-point increase. December tightening remains the central market expectation, although the precise probabilities have fluctuated as traders reassess growth risks and the inflationary impact of elevated energy prices. Treasury yields declined Thursday as selling in technology shares encouraged demand for government bonds. However, falling yields failed to support gold, suggesting that precious metals positioning, liquidation pressure and the outlook for further monetary tightening remained dominant considerations.
The Federal Reserve remains in its premeeting communications blackout, shifting attention to Friday's preliminary October manufacturing and services purchasing managers' indexes at 9:45 a.m. EDT and the final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey at 10 a.m. EDT. The reports will provide further evidence on business activity, consumer confidence and inflation expectations before next week's monetary policy decision.
The Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting and the subsequent release of September personal consumption expenditures inflation data on Oct. 29 will provide more substantial tests of market expectations for December tightening. Softer activity readings and easing inflation expectations could reduce pressure on yields and improve gold's outlook, while stronger economic data and persistent price pressures would reinforce the prospect of additional interest rate increases.
The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remained a significant source of financial-market uncertainty Thursday as renewed attacks on commercial shipping and energy infrastructure increased concerns about regional escalation. Reports of damaged vessels and threats to maritime traffic were accompanied by renewed security concerns involving Saudi Arabian energy facilities, while Washington and Tehran remained divided over the conditions for reopening normal commercial shipping through the strait. Diplomatic contacts have not produced a confirmed settlement, and uncertainty about possible additional military action has complicated efforts to stabilize the corridor. Although alternative pipelines, rerouting and ship-to-ship transfers have helped restore aggregate Middle Eastern oil exports, direct tanker movements through Hormuz remain substantially disrupted. The continuing security threat has sustained an elevated geopolitical risk premium in crude oil prices despite the partial recovery in regional exports.
For gold, the escalation presents competing influences. The prospect of further military confrontation supports defensive demand, but rising crude oil prices threaten to prolong inflation and increase pressure on the Fed to maintain restrictive monetary policy. Thursday's decline in gold despite lower Treasury yields highlights the limited effectiveness of traditional safe-haven support during the latest liquidation. Silver underperformed as the broader precious metals selloff coincided with weakening equity markets and concerns about industrial demand. The combination of high energy costs, slowing interest rate-sensitive activity and persistent inflation risks continues to complicate the outlook for both metals.
North American equity markets finished mixed to sharply lower Thursday as renewed selling in artificial intelligence-related shares overwhelmed gains in other sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 11.89 points, or less than 0.1%, to close at 52,867.98, while the S&P 500 lost 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43, its largest daily decline since July. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 694.00 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86, pressured by renewed concerns about the financing and profitability of artificial intelligence investment. The Russell 2000 gained 3.01 points, or approximately 0.11%, to 2,784.03. The contrast between heavy technology-sector losses and gains across a majority of individual stocks indicated that selling remained concentrated in highly valued growth shares rather than extending uniformly across the U.S. equity market.
European equity markets closed lower Thursday, pressured by rising crude oil prices, weaker corporate earnings sentiment and concerns about government finances. The pan-European Stoxx 600 declined approximately 1.05%, while Germany's DAX lost around 1.1%. France's CAC 40 fell approximately 1.4%, reflecting continuing fiscal uncertainty and pressure on French financial assets. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 declined approximately 0.3%, outperforming continental benchmarks, while Italy's FTSE MIB dropped roughly 2.5% and Spain's IBEX 35 lost approximately 2.1%. Banks, miners and other economically sensitive shares were among the weakest sectors as investors assessed the implications of higher energy prices and elevated borrowing costs for European economic growth.
The key outside markets see crude oil prices higher as renewed attacks and military threats involving Iran increase concerns about Middle Eastern energy exports. Brent crude traded above $113.00 a barrel during the U.S. session, while WTI approached $100.00. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note declined as demand for government bonds strengthened during the equity selloff. The U.S. dollar remained comparatively firm, while expectations for restrictive Fed policy continued to limit gold's ability to benefit from lower bond yields.( Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)
Technically, spot gold bulls' next upside price objective is to push prices back above the $4,068.00 to $4,079.00 resistance zone, with a sustained recovery targeting $4,124.25 and then $4,142.00. Bears' next near-term downside price objective is a break below $4,038.00, with additional downside risk if selling pressure persists. First resistance is seen at $4,068.00 and then at $4,079.00. First support is seen at $4,038.00, followed by the psychologically important $4,000.00 area.
Spot silver bulls' next upside price objective is to drive prices back above the $56.340 to $56.920 resistance zone, with a sustained move targeting $57.390 and then $57.870. The next downside price objective for the bears is a recovery failure below $54.750, with continued selling pressure leaving the metal vulnerable to additional weakness. articles.title_orig: iOS 27.1 is exclusive to iPhone Duo, here’s why
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.1 is exclusive to iPhone Duo, here’s why
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.1 has officially launched, but you wouldn’t know it by checking your iPhone’s Settings app. That’s because the latest iPhone update is exclusive to iPhone Duo.
Last night, Apple quietly released a major new software update for iPhone.
iOS 27.1 was pushed out over the air, and normally that would mean new features for everyone.
However, you won’t find iOS 27.1 by opening the Settings app and navigating to General ⇾ Software Update. Instead, iOS 27.0.1 will appear as the most recent update.
That’s because iOS 27.1 is exclusive to the new iPhone Duo.
It’s an unusual move, but Apple decided to skip iOS 27.1 for most iPhone models and go straight to iOS 27.2 instead.
iOS 27.2 has been in beta testing for the last month and ships to all users next week . It includes new features like:
So why did Apple ship iOS 27.1 for iPhone Duo only?
Even though the iPhone Duo was officially unveiled last month, there are plenty of features and details we’ve only recently learned about. Bypassing a beta cycle for iOS 27.1 meant Apple was able to keep many of those details hidden until the Duo’s official launch.
Additionally, there were likely engineering reasons why it was simpler on Apple’s end to keep iOS 27.1 separate and Duo-exclusive. There are all kinds of custom iOS designs and features that the Duo introduces, and it’s expected that managing all of that internally was easier without other models or new features in the mix.
So next week when your iPhone says iOS 27.2 is available to install, just know that you didn’t somehow miss iOS 27.1 entirely.
Have you been running the iOS 27.2 beta? How’s it running for you? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_orig: More than 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled nationwide: FDA
articles.title_zh: More than 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled nationwide: FDA
articles.content_orig:
On October 19, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an enforcement report announcing 17 Class II nationwide recalls of adults’ and kids’ toothpaste. The toothpaste was manufactured by Pritam International Private Limited and distributed in the U.S. by Ashtel Studios Inc. Pritam initiated the voluntary recall on September 10 for 4,301,700 tubes.
The FDA states that the reason for the recalls is Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) deviations . While specific details weren’t provided by the agency, CGMP regulations ensure that products—like anticavity toothpaste, which are regulated like OTC drugs—are made correctly and consistently.
A Class II recall means that if you’re exposed to or use a product, you could experience temporary or medically treatable adverse health problems, or that serious adverse health issues are unlikely. The enforcement report didn’t include any information as to whether any illnesses have been reported as linked to the recall.
There are a number of varieties of toothpaste being recalled, including popular kids’ toothpastes with characters like Barbie, Hot Wheels, Crayola Silly Scents, and My Little Pony. Adult toothpaste varieties include whitening, sensitivity, cavity-protection, and gum health formulas.
Check the toothpaste you have against the following list of recalled products, and check the FDA’s full list of affected products, including UPCs, lot numbers, and expiration dates.
The FDA hasn’t provided any specific instructions regarding what to do with the products, but because they are part of a recall, it’s safest to stop using them. You should contact the retailer or manufacturer for information regarding refunds.

articles.title_orig: Engineers perform delicate operation on explosives-packed World War II shipwreck, but bombs remain in place
articles.title_zh: Engineers perform delicate operation on explosives-packed World War II shipwreck, but bombs remain in place
articles.content_orig:
Sheerness, England — A delicate operation aimed at preventing an 82-year-old U.S. shipwreck packed with tons of World War II explosives from unleashing a potentially catastrophic tidal wave on London has been completed. But while the most imminent danger has been addressed, the explosives remain inside the rusting wreck of the SS Richard Montgomery on the riverbed, and experts aren't taking their eyes off it.
The Montgomery, one of about 2,700 Liberty ships built in the U.S. to support the Allied war effort, was grounded on a sandbar off the town of Sheerness in the Thames Estuary, just 40 miles from the British capital, in August 1944. It was carrying munitions intended to support the Allies following the D-Day landings.
The vessel broke apart during salvage efforts and sank, with an estimated 1,500 tons of explosives in its cargo holds.
The ship's three rusting masts protruding from the water had been a familiar sight to residents and passing vessels for decades. But recent surveys revealed increasing deterioration in the structure, raising fears the masts could collapse and trigger an explosion.
"The vessel was starting to lean and deteriorate, so they could see some of the structures around the mast starting to collapse," Nolan Conway, a naval architect with Florida-based marine salvage firm Resolve Marine Group, which was contracted to remove the masts, told CBS News.
"The fear is the masts could have fallen onto the cargo itself, causing it to detonate," he said. "Some of the munitions are believed to be fused munitions with pressure fuses, so something like an impact could potentially set them off."
U.K. maritime minister Keir Mather told lawmakers in the House of Commons this week that the "complex project requiring specialist program, engineering and risk management expertise" had been completed ahead of schedule and on budget, with all three of the masts removed at a cost of just under $13 million, according to The Guardian .
Mather said in the U.K. Parliament that the masts had put "significant load on the structure and their removal has reduced that risk and supports the long-term safe management of the site."
The government has long maintained an exclusion zone around the wreck, which is about 1.5 miles off the Sheerness coast.
Mather told lawmakers the wreck would "continue to be subject to continuous monitoring and control via the established exclusion zone."
Removing the remaining explosives would carry considerable risks, and the consequences of an explosion remain the subject of debate among experts.
"The impact of this wreck detonating is unpredictable," Conway said. "Estimates range from impacting the shoreline, to creating a tidal wave that could travel up the Thames, to a rather minor event that could potentially just close a nearby shipping channel. There's a large range of impacts, but none of them are really good."
Officials continue to assess the overall risk of an explosion as low, but the deteriorating condition of the masts prompted authorities to act.
Conway said the challenge for the firm was to devise a way to remove the masts without disturbing the sunken ship's hull and the perilous cargo inside, or putting the people doing the work at risk.
"How can you cut off that mast without vibrating or impacting the wreck?" he said. "We designed a custom lifting frame to safely pick it up without the mast swinging or swaying as we lifted it free of the wreck."
Engineers used a remotely operated underwater diamond-wire saw that clamps "around the mast with hydraulic arms and passes the saw through without getting divers in the water," Conway explained.
The removal of the masts marks the end of a distinctive chapter in the wreck's history. The masts, visible above the estuary since World War II, are expected to be preserved for public display.
Mather, the U.K. maritime minister, said the masts had been moved to a local museum, the Historic Dockyard Chatham, and would be displayed "in recognition of the historic significance of the SS Richard Montgomery and its role in supporting the Allied forces' efforts during World War II."
More than eight decades after the ship failed to reach the battlefields of Europe, the Montgomery and its dangerous cargo will remain where it came to rest, now entirely hidden from view, but far from forgotten.

articles.title_orig: New for Necromunda in 2027
articles.title_zh: New for Necromunda in 2027
articles.content_orig:
New for Necromunda in 2027
There’s an exciting year ahead for fans of Necromunda, with a lineup more stuffed than the questionably-sourced contents of a back-alley Scabber’s overcoat. There will be new miniatures, new terrain, new vehicles and new expansions. However, there won’t be a Roleplay expansion.
After careful consideration we’ve decided to focus our efforts on providing even more great minis for the core game.
Don’t worry – all the minis we showcased in the Big Autumn Preview are still on their way, and will be available for use in standard games of Necromunda.
Looking ahead to 2027, the new releases will cover multiple key gangs and locations, so here's a roadmap, because everybody loves roadmaps.*
Starting in the spring, we go back to the ash wastes with new rules expansions and the biggest plastic vehicle kit yet released for Necromunda.
Then, those brave enough can once more enter the cursed depths of the Underhells in search of ancient archeotech, where among other things they will bump into new Fighters for the Malstrain Genestealer cults.
And then we return to the still-smoking urban sprawl of Cinderak City, one of the conflict flashpoints of the recent Aranthian Succession . This is accompanied by support for some of the original underhive crews of Necromunda, including hulking new brutes.
And we’re still not done for 2027. Rounding out the year, there will be new mercenaries and gunslingers, set on hunting down their unfortunate bounties in whatever dank or irradiated corner of Necromunda they sought to hide.
Alongside all of the above, you’ll also get support for other gangs, scenery, and regular rules expansions.
And still set to arrive this year is a major expansion for the House of Iron in the shape of three flexible new multipart plastic kits, offering an enormous range of new cosmetic and wargear options for your Orlock gang.
We’ll cover them all in more detail soon, so check back regularly, and sign up to the Warhammer newsletter to stay up to date with the latest Necromunda news.
* Everybody except the Ash Waste Nomads, but they just hate roads!

articles.title_orig: Romania blames Russia for drone that sinks cargo ship; 1 killed, 3 missing
articles.title_zh: Romania blames Russia for drone that sinks cargo ship; 1 killed, 3 missing
articles.content_orig:
Romania has blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast, killing one crew member and leaving three others missing.
It’s the latest drone attack targeting commercial shipping off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria, with at least seven cargo ships hit and 30 sailors reported killed or missing in the past two weeks, raising fears of an escalation in Russia’s war against Ukraine.
The drone struck the Comoros-flagged vessel Khoryv and its crew of 13 Ukrainian and Azeri sailors on Friday, 13 nautical miles (24km) off Romania’s port of Constanta, just outside Romania’s territorial waters.
The shipping data website MarineTraffic showed the Khoryv departed Turkiye on Wednesday and was headed for Romania’s Sulina port, which links the Danube River to the Black Sea.
The canal has become the primary ‌‌‌‌route for Ukrainian exporters, which rely on ports on the Danube and Romanian territorial waters, as Russia has ‌‌‌‌attacked ‌‌‌‌Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports.
Video released by Romanian authorities showed only a small part of the hull of the capsized tanker still visible above ⁠⁠⁠⁠the waves as it sank.
Romania launched a rescue operation after the Khoryv sent a distress signal about 10am local time (0700 GMT).
Nine sailors were rescued, three were missing and one body was recovered during a search and rescue operation hampered by poor weather conditions and low visibility, Romania’s naval authority said.
Ukraine, Romania and Bulgaria have called on NATO to “fast-track the additional surveillance capabilities” to protect commercial shipping, after a surge in Black Sea drone attacks as fighting in Russia’s war on Ukraine escalates. NATO said on Tuesday that it would send more maritime patrol aircraft , radar systems and drones to the ⁠⁠⁠⁠Black Sea.
Romanian and European officials blamed Russia for the attack, which Romania’s President Nicusor Dan called “a new example of the tragic consequences of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine”.
“It is time for Russia to take peace initiatives of the United States and Europe seriously, accept the ceasefire proposals and end the war,” he said.
Romania’s Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said on Facebook that the attack was “unacceptable and constitutes a flagrant violation of international law”.
Moldova’s Foreign Ministry posted on X that “Russia’s continued escalation in the Black Sea endangers civilian lives, threatens freedom of navigation and undermines regional security”.
EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the attacks “reckless”, which “target innocent lives and openly defy international law.”
Russian officials did not immediately publicly comment on Friday’s sinking. It occurred after Romanian warplanes shot down two of ⁠⁠⁠⁠the latest-generation Russian drones over Romanian territorial ⁠⁠⁠⁠waters on Saturday. Russia has previously denied it is responsible for deadly drone attacks in the region.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 22, 2026, Bloom Energy ( BE -12.75% ) raised its full-year revenue outlook to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion, up from $3.9 billion to $4.2 billion. Surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence data centers is pushing commercial customers toward on-site fuel cell generation. Three takeaways from management explain why this shift matters for long-term investors.
Management upgraded full-year revenue guidance for the third time this year, projecting 2026 growth of about 122% at the midpoint versus last year. It's seeing customer demand for rapidly deployable on-site power drive backlog growth faster than current shipments can keep up with.
Quarterly revenue reached $1.24 billion while operating expenses grew at a much slower pace. That discipline expanded operating margins and generated $286 million in non-GAAP operating income, a measure of profit from core business operations.
An American Electric Power contract for 700 megawatts of server capacity showcases how utilities are using on-site generation at the front of the meter, or directly on distribution networks. Integrating carbon capture and sequestration (CCS), which traps emissions before they escape, opens a trillion-dollar market opportunity.
Demand for on-site electricity is surging as data centers outgrow traditional grid infrastructure. Bloom is expanding manufacturing capacity while maintaining pricing discipline to fund its growth.
As global power requirements rise, on-site fuel cells offer faster deployment than utility grids. That structural advantage positions Bloom Energy to lead a transformation in energy delivery.

articles.title_orig: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.title_zh: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.content_orig:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda , Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
The new information contradicts accounts from Uganda, which previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo, and will raise concerns about the ability of authorities to contain the outbreak, which is already the most geographically widespread in history.
The Ugandan government reported Ebola cases in May and June before WHO declared it Ebola-free in August. A Ugandan government spokesperson told Reuters on Thursday that Uganda had no ​Ebola cases and that, if ​it did, it would make that information ​public.
The World Health Organization said investigations were continuing to establish the likely source of infection for the Ebola patient in Nigeria.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating whether the patient may have come into contact with an Ebola patient in Kenya, as both travelled from Uganda’s Entebbe airport on 3 October, said Dr Wessam Mankoula, head of emergency preparedness and response at the organisation.
Catherine Smallwood, a WHO Ebola incident manager in DR Congo, told a UN briefing in Geneva via video ‌link on Friday that WHO staff in DR Congo had no information showing the patient in Nigeria had travelled to the country.
Smallwood said a link to the case in Kenya was possible, ​but added that officials would need to compare the timing with when the Nigeria patient’s symptoms began to tell whether the infection more likely happened at the Ugandan airport or elsewhere.
Marion Koopmans, a Dutch virologist and member of the WHO’s Ebola emergency committee, cast doubt on the theory. “I think that is very speculative unless there is evidence of sharing the same ​space in a manner that could explain that,” she said. “Random presence at the same location, a large airport, is not a supported epidemiological link by any standard of what we currently know.”
The Nigerian health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate, said Nigeria’s case remains contained and that contact-tracing was continuing. “We are trying to contain it so it doesn’t go out to the communities. Hopefully, it won’t get to that and we are working hard to ensure that,” Pate said.
Melaku Yirga, vice-president for Africa at Prosper Global (formerly Mercy Corps), said the confirmation of Ebola in Kenya and Nigeria reinforces the need for countries to work closely together to prevent further transmission.
“What matters most now is speed, sharing information across borders without delay and ensuring frontline health workers and local organiaations have the resources to respond quickly,” he said.
Ebola is a highly contagious and often fatal viral disease that affects humans and non-human primates. It spreads through body fluids or contaminated materials and causes organ damage, blood vessel impairment and sometimes severe internal and external bleeding.
The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine. It was first announced on 15 May and has infected more than 9,500 people and killed nearly half of them.
The outbreak is the largest and deadliest in DR Congo’s history and second only ​globally to ​the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa, which infected ​more than ‌28,600 people ​and ​killed more than 11,000.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed reporting

A tsunami alert has been issued in Italy after a series of tremors was detected off the Mediterranean coast.
As many as 12 quakes were recorded with magnitudes of up to 5.0 near Sicily on Friday lunchtime, prompting precautionary evacuations of schools in Palermo and Messina.
An orange tsunami alert was issued for residents to vigilant and exercise caution around coastal areas as students left classes and public offices were abandoned, according to local media.
A courthouse was evacuated as far away as Trapani, on the west coast, while students and municipal workers vacated buildings in Lipari, an island between Sicily and mainland Italy.
The epicentre was less than 60 miles from Palermo, on the northern coastline, which has a population of 648,260 as the island’s capital.
Locals reported feeling tremors in Palermo, Patti, Licata, Capo dʿOrlando and Campofelice di Roccella. Licata is 180km from the epicentre.
The other 11 tremors all registered above 3.0-magnitude, officials said.
The United States Geological Survey recorded a 5.7 magnitude quake at a depth of 10km north of the island, occurring at 10:19am local time.
At the time of writing, there were no reports of injuries or damage to property.
Palermo mayor Roberto Lagalla said the authorities were closely monitoring an evolving situation.
“Currently, no reports of damage to people or property have been received, but we believe it is our duty to take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of our citizens,” he said in a statement.
“The possible evacuation of some public buildings is purely precautionary, dictated by the need to act promptly and prudently.”
He urged residents and people near the coast stay away from the sea and follow the instructions of the relevant authorities.
Did you feel the earthquake? Contact james.reynolds@independent.co.uk
The Sicilian city of Marsala and neighbouring towns were struck by a tornado earlier this month in what experts said was an almost unprecedented event for the Mediterranean island.
Vehicles were overturned and two people were seriously injured on October 9 as the whirlwind swept through, destroying a house and damaging a school and other buildings.
“It was almost like an American tornado, nothing this violent has been seen in living memory,” the head of Sicily's civil protection agency Salvatore Cocina told Reuters.
Early in September the agency issued a warning saying the sweltering summer had led to a buildup of heat that could trigger extreme weather events in autumn.

China’s domestic online beauty sales are falling as C-beauty companies are ramping up export efforts and moving into international retail channels. The gap suggests a deliberate pivot from C-beauty toward overseas growth, targeting the categories and regions that K-beauty has spent the past decade winning over.
According to Jefferies’ China online beauty tracker , the country recorded a 6% year-on-year cosmetics sales decline in September 2026. Skin care fell 6.1%, while color cosmetics went down 5.2%.
However, at the same time, data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) shows China climbing from seventh place to fifth in global cosmetics exports. The trade body says China’s color cosmetics exports amount to nearly three times that of Korea’s.
C-beauty company Proya, meanwhile, has opened a European Innovation Center Laboratory in France and has announced it will begin selling across 400 Ulta Beauty stores in the US next month.
“This Europe Innovation Center Laboratory connects the European and Chinese ecosystems to draw on combined strengths and create new innovation capabilities,” says Hou Juncheng, founder and chairman of Proya Cosmetics.
The center is not the first bridge between Chinese and European beauty. French ingredient suppliers have been actively pursuing partnerships with Chinese cosmetics brands, and many Chinese perfumers train in France. The country’s Cosmetic Valley, meanwhile, has set up a Shanghai-based fragrance and cosmetics embassy to encourage collaboration between the two markets . Chinese beauty brands are expanding overseas, targeting markets where K-beauty has established a strong presence.
With color cosmetics exports already outpacing Korea’s and a growing foothold in US and European retail, C-beauty appears to be borrowing the playbook that got K-beauty onto global shelves.
The September figures from Jefferies’ tracker show many multinational beauty giants experiencing declining figures in China. L’Oréal fell 5%, Estée Lauder 8%, Procter & Gamble 20%, Shiseido 24%, and LVMH 26%.
Beiersdorf and Galderma were the only multinationals to grow, supported by their Nivea and Cetaphil brands. At the brand level, dermatological skin care like CeraVe and Cetaphil grew (35% and 58%, respectively), while Bobbi Brown fell 31%. Among domestic players, Mao Geping grew 26%, and Proya grew 1%.
As demand becomes increasingly selective, and derma-brands gain ground, Jefferies’ findings show skin care and color cosmetics accounting for over 80% of China’s beauty market. Both categories initially gave rise to K-beauty.
According to KITA, China’s cosmetic exports reached ₩8.14 trillion (US$6.1 billion) from January to July 2026, up 24% from ₩6.55 trillion (US$4.9 billion) a year earlier. The figures lifted China to fifth in global export rankings, behind France in the lead and South Korea in second place.
In color cosmetics, China has already overtaken Korea. Exports of lip and eye makeup, powders, and nail products totaled ₩1.88 trillion (US$1.41 billion) from January to July, about 2.9 times Korea’s ₩644.7 billion (US$484 million).
From January to July 2026, China’s lip makeup exports were 1.7 times Korea’s, and its eye makeup exports were 3.5 times. China’s exports grew 17% to 33% across all four color cosmetics categories (lip, eye, powders, and nail products), while Korea’s lip makeup and nail product exports fell 15% and 15.6%, respectively. Proya is expanding its international presence with a new research laboratory in France.
According to The Asia Business Daily, Kecia Steelman, CEO of Ulta Beauty, raised C-beauty during the company’s 2026 Q2 fiscal earnings call. She is quoted as saying, “[We are launching] Proya, the number one skin care brand in China. So it’s not just about K-Beauty anymore.”
Proya’s US launch will be the first time a Chinese premium skin care brand joins Ulta’s online and physical networks at the same time. The rollout is planned for November this year, and with it, Proya says it is “moving beyond mere product export to brand globalization.”
To expand, the company says, “brands must not only enter overseas markets but also earn a permanent place in consumers’ daily skin care regimens and secure a voice within elite global beauty narratives.”
Securing that voice, Proya has inaugurated its Europe Innovation Center Laboratory in France, with a 450 square meter site containing 76 pieces of equipment and seven dedicated researchers. The lab will focus on research and innovation in skin longevity, biology, biotechnology, and sustainable ingredients.
The lab will collaborate with the Hangzhou Longwu center in China, which handles formulation, ingredients, safety, and efficacy, and the Shanghai center, which works on hair care and the scalp microbiome.
Proya’s international push comes after its namesake brand, which accounts for around 70% of group revenue, posted a 7% sales decline in H1 2026. The drop was the company’s first after years of uninterrupted growth since its 2017 Shanghai listing. Jefferies says the brand returned to 1% growth in September, but the overseas expansion appears partly aimed at offsetting soft momentum.

articles.title_zh: All lanes open after deadly crash in Durham creates severe delays on I-40, I-885 near RDU
articles.content_orig:
A busy stretch of Interstate 40 East near Raleigh-Durham International Airport reopened Friday morning several hours after Durham police found a woman who was hit by multiple unknown vehicles.
Durham police said they responded to a call about a pedestrian being hit on I-40 near Davis Drive around 1:30 a.m. When they arrived, they found the woman dead and said she had been hit multiple times by unknown vehicles.
The eastbound lanes of I-40 were closed for a mile from Exit 280 at Davis Drive to Exit 281 to South Miami Boulevard. The severe delays extended onto Interstate 885 as well.
At 8 a.m., a lane had reopened on I-40 and traffic was flowing again. All lanes on I-40 reopened by 8:30 a.m.
Hours before the morning commute, WRAL Breaking News Tracker arrived before 4 a.m. to find multiple officers blocking the interstate for an investigation. Police would not let reporters near the scene.
WRAL's Shaun Gallagher arrived at 6 a.m. as the backup worsened. According to Gallagher, the miles of backups on the road resembled 8:30 a.m. rush hour instead of the usual 6 a.m. traffic.
Sky 5 flew over the delays at 7:15 a.m., showing miles and miles of traffic.
Police said they cannot release any other information about the investigation at this time.
